title: Pee Wee Erwin takes over as leader at Nick's
summary: Pee Wee Erwin became leader when Hackett was busy, and Leeman and Hinton praise him as a trumpeter and person.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Well, the story behind that is I worked there for a year and a half -- let's see, we're getting into the fifties -- between '50 and '51, Bobby was very busy doing other things, so Pee Wee Erwin took his place as the leader, he became our leader -- and there's a great traditional man.
Oh, what a man. Anything you want to say nice, just include it and wrap it all up in one package and say Pee Wee Erwin, and that's it Dizzy. That's right. Tommy Dorsey, all the great bands ...
I don't know whether he's a greater trumpet player or a greater person. It goes together.

Well, he is going through exactly what you and I have gone through, Cliff, and that is all of these eras, and he's played all of them and he's played them all well, and he's still playing today like you and I are, and we are most grateful for his presence.
